source: The survey's Evaluation section: the table 'Evaluation taxonomy' and the figure 'Evaluating proactiveness requires evidence beyond task completion'

levels.name: Task Utility
levels.question: Does proactive assistance improve overall task outcomes?
levels.purpose: Establishes whether an intervention improves outcomes.

categories.name: Task Success
metrics: Goal completion rate against reference or verifiable outcomes
Domain-specific task outcomes
Per-intervention (turn-level) success rate

categories.name: Task Efficiency
metrics: Agent computational cost: latency, tokens, triggering frequency
User interaction cost: turns, interruptions, correction effort
Quality-adjusted efficiency: benefit per unit cost

levels.name: Mechanism-Level
levels.question: How does the agent decide what, when, and how to act?
levels.purpose: Examines how effectively the underlying capacities operate.

categories.name: Context Modeling Efficacy
metrics: Retrieval precision and recall over long or multimodal context
Knowledge-update accuracy and stale-information rate
Context efficiency
Pre-decision evidence coverage

categories.name: User State and World State Anticipation
metrics: Intent, goal, and preference accuracy
Prediction lead time and false-alarm rate
Ambiguity-detection F1 and clarification utility
Next-state and event-forecast accuracy

categories.name: Planning Quality
metrics: Objective and agenda-selection accuracy
Plan validity and subgoal coverage
Constraint satisfaction and preference utility
Plan-revision success under new constraints

categories.name: Intervention Decision and Timing
metrics: Intervention precision, recall, and F1 (act, ask, defer, or abstain)
Autonomy calibration: deferral accuracy, risk–coverage
Trigger-timing accuracy
Unwanted-initiative or persistence-after-rejection rate

categories.name: Intervention Delivery and Presentation
metrics: Content correctness and execution accuracy
Delivery-mode appropriateness relative to risk and reversibility
Comprehension and legibility of agent intent
Editability, cancellation, and reversal success

categories.name: Adaptation and Generalization
metrics: Personalization gain and learning efficiency
Recovery speed and stale-memory rate under drift
Generalization to unseen users, tasks, or environments

levels.name: User Experience
levels.question: How does proactive assistance affect the user?
levels.purpose: Assesses effects on workload, control, and trust.

categories.name: User Workload
metrics: Subjective workload: NASA-TLX, Workload Profile, SWAT
Behavioral disruption: interpretation time, recovery time, task-switch cost
Net effort removed vs. newly introduced

categories.name: Usability and Experience
metrics: Standardized usability and UX scores: SUS, UEQ
Perceived usefulness, naturalness, and collaboration quality
Intrusiveness and privacy concern

categories.name: Level of Control
metrics: Perceived agency and preferred autonomy level
Override, modification, and reversal success rate
Gap between formal and effective control

categories.name: Trust and Reliance
metrics: Trust-in-automation scales, calibrated to actual reliability
Appropriate reliance: correct-accept and correct-reject rate
Critical-engagement behavior: verification, error detection
Longitudinal trust trajectory
